source.title: Decompose Sparsely Where You Should, Absorb Densely Where You Should No
source.authors: Rui-Xuan Deng; Ze-Hao Jin; Ze-Kun Wang; Zi-Han Dong

page_placements.theme: Low-rank components can capture important information or correct functional loss

record.tranche_reason: The study reports that its rank-24 bottleneck does not substantially reduce SAE dark matter, suggesting it may be distinct from the low-rank scaffold studied here. This is a refinement of the proposed training-artifact explanation, not a direct test of the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study discusses prior work on linearly predictable SAE error but does not itself measure linear predictability, error-norm scaling across SAE sizes, or whether SAE reconstruction errors are unusually harmful. Its own bottleneck, dense-latent, loss, and topic results concern a related scaffold, not those claim versions. The dark-matter statement in Section 6.4 is the one reported result that directly bears on V6.
record.test_reason: The study mainly concerns a low-rank scaffold and dense latents, not dark matter. Its one result on dark matter is that an architectural change (a parallel rank-24 linear bottleneck) that improves EV does not substantially reduce Engels et al.'s dark matter (Section 6.4). Table 2 reports a column labelled FVUnl that falls only from .106 to .100 at r=24. This bears weakly on V6's claim that better architectures shrink dark matter. It is a side observation with no detailed protocol.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that residual streams contain a compact, low-rank, causally critical component that sparse dictionaries represent inefficiently. In open questions they note that Engels et al.'s dark matter is not substantially reduced by the bottleneck and may be a distinct form of scaffold.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds a parallel rank-24 linear bottleneck and investigates dense latents, scaffold removal, and sparse encoding; it does not reproduce the cited dark-matter error analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Bottleneck effects on SAE metrics vary by architecture; the dense-latent reduction differs between BatchTopK and Matryoshka. The dark-matter statement is qualitative and does not specify a separate condition or measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: The rank-24 bottleneck cuts dense-latent counts (25 to 4 on BatchTopK, 69 to 44 on Matryoshka) and removes the classifiable dense-latent categories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low-rank parallel linear channel absorbs most classifiable persistent dense SAE latents.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting out the learned 24-d scaffold raises CE from 1.90 to 14.3 (BatchTopK) or 13.8 (Matryoshka). Removing the top-24 PCA directions raises it to 5.37. A random 24-d removal has negligible effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned low-rank residual-stream component is causally important beyond the top PCs.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating 787 aligned SAE features raises CE only to 5.5. Topic information sits compactly in the 24 bottleneck dimensions but is spread redundantly across sparse atoms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionaries encode the low-rank scaffold redundantly rather than compactly.

record.problems: The experiments use a single model and layer, as the authors acknowledge. The dark-matter result is stated qualitatively without a numerical measure, detailed protocol, or uncertainty in the presented text. The scaffold interventions do not directly measure SAE reconstruction error.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of SAE error from the input is not measured.
Error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, shared failing contexts, and non-vanishing with scale are not tested. Dictionary size is fixed at 16,384.
Spliced-in SAE reconstruction versus random error of equal norm is not tested.
Whether the linear error part holds unlearned features and the nonlinear part resists larger dictionaries is not tested. The bottleneck is not a dictionary-size scaling.
Circuit or steering analyses with and without the error term are not tested. The scaffold ablations remove a learned subspace, not the SAE error.
The roles of the sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents and end-to-end objectives are not tested. Only one architectural add-on is tested, on one model and one layer.

missing.what: FVUnl values across the BatchTopK rank sweep: .106, .104, .102, .100, .096, .090 for r=0 to 96, and .000 at r=2304. This is the only numerical dark-matter-like measure in the paper. It shows a slow, small decline with bottleneck rank.

record.verdict_notes: The dark-matter bearing is incidental. The bottleneck is designed to absorb the top-variance PCs, not dark matter, so failing to reduce dark matter only weakly challenges V6's 'better architectures shrink it' strand. FVUnl is not defined in the text, so treating it as Engels' nonlinear error fraction is an inference. The study uses a single model and layer, with no seeds reported for these numbers. Rows r2–r11 are correctly linked to none.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, shared failing contexts across sizes, and whether error vanishes with scale.
Whether SAE reconstructions harm loss more than random errors of equal size.
Whether the linear component contains unlearned SAE features and the nonlinear component resists further dictionary learning.
Whether analyses of circuits or steering lose behavior when the SAE error term is omitted.

The study does not test the proposed roles of sparsity penalties, shrinkage, dead latents, or objective choice; nor does it test end-to-end training. Its dark-matter statement concerns only whether this study's bottleneck substantially reduces it.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, BatchTopK SAE (16k, L0=40) with a parallel rank-24 linear bottleneck
relationships.reason: The authors state that dark matter is not substantially reduced by the bottleneck. Table 2 shows FVUnl only .106 to .100 despite higher EV (r1). The evidence is weak: one add-on architecture, the metric is undefined, and there is no uncertainty reported.
relationships.display_finding: Adding the linear bottleneck changed FVUnl only from 0.106 to 0.100 despite increasing explained variance.
